page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton2 processors. The configuration features 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs based on the ARM64 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture operating at 2.5 GHz. Each physical core has 64 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache, backed by 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory density is the defining feature of this instance, providing 512.0 GB of total RAM, which translates to an expansive 1:16 vCPU-to-memory ratio (16.0 GB per vCPU). The host does not include a dedicated GPU accelerator, but bundles 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable multi-threaded performance alongside deliberate architectural tradeoffs. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 17385.11 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 11488.0, placing overall multi-threaded compute in the middle 50% tier. In contrast, single-threaded metrics skew lower; single-core Geekbench scores reach 942.0 and single-thread bzip3 decompression yields 7.26 GB/sec, falling into lower benchmark percentiles due to the moderate 2.5 GHz clock frequency and absence of x86 vector extensions like AVX-512. Memory throughput is solid across uncached read and write benchmarks (139.81 GB/sec read and 70.12 GB/sec write on 256 MB blocks), while Redis SET operations sustain 36.44 million operations per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the Graviton2 processor architecture yields significant cost and resource advantages for memory-bound applications. The inclusion of bundled 1900 GB local NVMe storage provides rapid scratch space or high-speed caching without incurring network-attached storage overheads. The instance is primarily suited for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caches, Apache Spark or Hadoop memory-heavy clusters, Electronic Design Automation (EDA), and heavy transactional database workloads that require massive memory footprints but do not depend on high single-thread clock speeds.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs on the ARM64 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 architecture at 2.5 GHz. It delivers 512.0 GB of memory (a 1:16 vCPU-to-RAM ratio), 1900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, and 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. With no dedicated GPU, its hardware design is focused on workloads with large memory working sets. Benchmarks place multi-threaded compute, Redis throughput (36.44 million SET operations per second), and memory bandwidth within average percentiles, though single-core throughput reflects the lower clock frequency of the Graviton2 core. By combining high memory capacity with bundled high-speed NVMe storage and power-efficient ARM architecture, the x2gd.8xlarge offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for in-memory databases, large-scale caching, big data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
